conclusions.summary: Both C.1 build failures (Conversations and NewPipe) share the exact same demonstrated root cause: upstream AGP/R8 resource shrinking left orphaned attribute references in precompiled library XML files while deleting the attribute definitions from resources.arsc. Apktool 2.10.0 omits undeclared ARSC attributes from attrs.xml, causing AAPT2 link failure. Newer Apktool 3.0.3 resolves this by synthesizing missing attrs, achieving 100% build success on both apps.
recommendations_for_c2: Support Apktool 3.0.3 or higher in the BuildService to natively handle R8 resource-shrunk applications.
Ensure the Android 35 SDK framework (platforms/android-35/android.jar) is always installed in the build environment to resolve modern Android 15 manifest/style attributes.

For Apktool 2.x compatibility fallback, BuildService can implement a pre-link attribute synthesis step that injects <attr name="..."> into res/values/attrs.xml for any orphaned attributes reported by AAPT2.
Preserve native libraries directly (as validated, Apktool already preserves native .so files byte-for-byte).
Account for expected binary differences in DEX and ARSC during semantic verification (exact SHA-256 matching of DEX/ARSC is impossible after decompilation).
